items.mainDefect: Async legacy writes inherit request cancellation and can fail when the HTTP handler returns.

secondary.defect: Legacy write errors are recorded only in metrics and are never logged.

items.mainDefect: Legacy Update recomputes the updated object against legacy state instead of persisting the unified-store result.

secondary.defect: UpdatedObjectInfo is invoked a second time asynchronously even though its implementation may not be safe or idempotent.

items.mainDefect: Delete success metrics use the object name as the kind label, causing inconsistent labels and unbounded cardinality.

secondary.defect: Delete injects the bare logger into the context, losing the enriched name, kind, and method fields.

items.mainDefect: Async legacy writes inherit the request context and can be canceled when the handler returns.

secondary.defect: Returning before the legacy write completes removes the completion-on-return guarantee relied on by legacy readers and migration logic.
Background legacy write failures are invisible to callers and are not logged.

items.mainDefect: Passing raw objInfo to legacy Update allows it to persist a different object from unified storage.

secondary.defect: Calling UpdatedObject twice breaks UpdatedObjectInfo implementations that are not idempotent.

items.mainDefect: The background legacy write inherits request cancellation, allowing it to be aborted before its timeout.

secondary.defect: Legacy write failures are only recorded in metrics and never logged.

items.mainDefect: Legacy Update recomputes the object from legacy state instead of writing the exact unified-store result.

secondary.defect: Unordered asynchronous updates can reach legacy storage in reverse order and leave it permanently stale.
